description: `default` (uses dockremap user) or `<user>:<group>`. Daemon still runs as root; container root maps to a non-zero host uid. Mutually exclusive with --privileged, --ipc=host, --net=host, --pid=host containers.
Default seccomp profile. `builtin` = moby's default.json (~44 syscalls blocked). Path = custom JSON. `unconfined` = no seccomp.
Enable SELinux container labeling. Requires SELinux running in enforcing/permissive on host.
Set the no_new_privs bit by default for new containers. Stops setuid binaries from gaining new caps.
Default cgroup-namespace mode. Private hides host's cgroup tree from container.
Default IPC namespace mode.
Daemon-wide ulimit defaults. Use to enforce nofile/nproc caps as a hardening baseline.
Daemon's OOM-killer preference. -500 keeps dockerd alive when host is memory-pressured.
Re-keyed under daemon.json-security to flag the security implication: experimental features may have weaker security review. Engine catalogues the canonical key.
Inter-container communication on default bridge. `false` enforces network isolation by default — containers must use user-defined networks (which are scoped) for comms.
Disabling docker-proxy reduces attack surface (one fewer suid-like helper) at the cost of breaking some hairpin/loopback patterns.
Authorization plugins (e.g. opa-docker-authz). Daemon refuses ops not allowed by every listed plugin. Useful for gating `docker run --privileged` etc. at the API.
Registries dockerd will talk to over HTTP / with self-signed TLS. Adds attack surface — restrict to your private registry CIDRs.
Keep containers running across daemon restart. Security note: an attacker who can crash/restart dockerd can't drop the running container's state.
Mark the daemon as running in rootless mode. Set by `dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh`. Affects defaults: e.g. snapshotter falls back to fuse-overlayfs on older kernels.
Parent cgroup. Pin to `system.slice/docker.slice` for systemd integration; required for full cgroup-delegation in rootless+systemd.
Includes `native.cgroupdriver=systemd` (single-writer rule for systemd hosts; security relevance: prevents cgroup conflicts that can lead to resource-limit bypass).
Prometheus metrics endpoint. Bind to loopback (`127.0.0.1:9323`); exposing on `0.0.0.0` is an info-leak surface.
Daemon listen sockets. Re-keyed here to flag: TCP without TLS is rejected by the daemon; mTLS mandatory for any TCP exposure.
Unix group owning the docker.sock. Membership = root-equivalent (mount host fs in a container, escape). Treat as sudo membership.

Action taken on syscalls not matched by syscalls[]. Values: SCMP_ACT_KILL, SCMP_ACT_KILL_PROCESS, SCMP_ACT_TRAP, SCMP_ACT_ERRNO[(errno)], SCMP_ACT_TRACE[(ret)], SCMP_ACT_ALLOW, SCMP_ACT_LOG, SCMP_ACT_NOTIFY. Docker default uses SCMP_ACT_ERRNO (deny+EPERM).
Architectures the filter applies to. e.g. `["SCMP_ARCH_X86_64","SCMP_ARCH_X86","SCMP_ARCH_X32"]` for amd64.

type: list[{names, action, args, errnoRet, comment, includes, excludes}]
description: Per-syscall rule list. names[] of syscall names; action; optional args[] for parameter-matching; errnoRet for SCMP_ACT_ERRNO. includes/excludes gate by minKernel/caps.
Syscall name list (NOT numbers). e.g. `["open","openat","openat2"]`.
Override action for this syscall set. Most common in default profile: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW.
Argument-matching rule. e.g. for socket(domain=…), `{index:0, value:AF_VSOCK, op:SCMP_CMP_EQ}` blocks vsock specifically while allowing other socket calls.
errno returned when action=SCMP_ACT_ERRNO. Default 1 (EPERM); commonly EACCES, ENOSYS for compat shimming.
Free-text. Conventional in default profile to document WHY a syscall is blocked.
Apply this rule only if container has these capabilities / runs on these arches / minKernel match. e.g. allow `mount` only if CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
Skip this rule under these conditions. Inverse of includes.
Permit syscall. Used for the bulk of allowlist entries.
Return EPERM (or errnoRet) without invoking syscall. Default action of moby's default profile.
Kill the calling thread. Brutal but unambiguous.
Log the syscall + allow it. Monitor mode for testing new profiles before flipping to ERRNO/KILL.
Notify a ptrace tracer; tracer can override return value (or kill). Used by sandboxes like nsjail / firejail.
Top-level profile declaration. Docker's default is `docker-default`. Custom: `profile docker-nginx flags=(attach_disconnected,mediate_deleted) { ... }`.
Profile flags. `attach_disconnected` = disconnected files mediated as parent; `mediate_deleted` = deleted files still mediated; `complain` = log without enforcing.

Allow a capability. e.g. `capability chown,`. Default profile allows: chown, dac_override, fowner, fsetid, kill, setgid, setuid, setpcap, net_bind_service, net_raw, sys_chroot, mknod, audit_write, setfcap.
Allow / deny network traffic by family + socket type. e.g. `network inet tcp,` or `deny network raw,`.
Path-based access. Permissions: r=read, w=write, x=execute, l=link, k=lock, m=memory-map, ix=inherit-x, mr=mmap-read, k=lock, w=write. e.g. `/var/run/nginx.pid w,`. Globs `**`/`*`/`?`.
Allow specific mount/umount operations. Most container profiles deny mount entirely; default allows umount.
Signal-sending policy. e.g. `signal (send) set=(term,kill) peer=other-profile,`.
ptrace permission. Default: deny (with selective allows for same-profile).
D-Bus messaging policy. Rare in container profiles.
AF_UNIX socket access policy.
Permission to switch to another profile mid-process. Highly restricted in container profiles.
Enable TLS + client cert verification (mTLS). dockerd refuses to start with TCP listener but no `--tlsverify`.
Enable TLS without client verification. Implied by --tlsverify.
CA cert chain. With --tlsverify, only client certs signed by this CA are accepted.
Daemon's server cert (or client's if on the CLI side).
Private key matching tlscert.
daemon.json forms equivalent to the CLI flags. Conflict between daemon.json and CLI flags = daemon refuses to start.
Any non-empty value enables mTLS on the client.
Dir containing ca.pem, cert.pem, key.pem on the client.
Conventional port for TLS-on TCP. 2375 = unencrypted (refused on modern dockerd).
The CN/SAN of the client cert maps to a 'user' in some authorization plugins. Useful for per-user policy on the daemon API.
Set to `1` to enable DCT for `pull`, `push`, `build`, `create`, `run`. With it on, pulls reject unsigned tags; pushes auto-sign.
Notary server URL. Override for self-hosted Notary.
Passphrase for the per-repo (tagging) key. Required for non-interactive signing in CI.
Passphrase for the offline (root) key. Should be supplied only during root-key ceremonies, not in CI.
Passphrase for the targets-of-targets key.
Optional basic-auth credentials for Notary server access (private notary instances).
Generic passphrase for any trust key being loaded via `docker trust key load`.
Local trust store: private keys under `private/<sha256>.key`, TUF metadata under `tuf/<server>/<repo>/`.
Human-readable name for a delegation. Used in `docker trust key generate <name>` and `docker trust signer add <name> <gun>`. Surfaced in `docker trust inspect --pretty`.
Notary's term for a fully-qualified image repo. Format: `<registry-host>/<repo>` (no tag). Each GUN has its own trust-data tree.
`/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid` line format. e.g. `testuser:231072:65536` = uids 231072..296607 mapped into the user's namespace as 0..65535. Multi-range allowed (max 5 entries per kernel limit).
Per docs, you need ≥ 65,536 subordinate UIDs/GIDs for the user (one per possible container uid/gid).
With `userns-remap: "default"`, dockerd creates the `dockremap` user + group and uses their subuid/subgid ranges.
`/proc/<pid>/uid_map` and gid_map accept at most 5 entries. Docker will use only the first 5 ranges if the file has more.
Distro tool to manage subuid/subgid ranges. e.g. `usermod --add-subuids 100000-165535 alice`.
Per-user runtime dir for sockets/pidfiles. Cleaned at logout — `loginctl enable-linger <user>` keeps it across logouts for persistent rootless services.
Socket path of the rootless dockerd. The setuptool prints it in the install output.
Setuptool reminds: `export PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH` so the user's `docker` CLI picks up the right binary.
Rootless networking backend.
Port-forward driver. `builtin` (default) uses RootlessKit's port driver; `slirp4netns` uses slirp4netns's built-in port forwarder.
MTU for rootless network. Lower for VPN-tunneled hosts.
Disable container access to host loopback (security hardening — containers can't reach host services on 127.0.0.1).
Rootless containerd's grpc socket. Distinct from the system-wide /run/containerd/containerd.sock.
Bootstrap script that creates the user-mode systemd service, configures CLI context `rootless`, and reminds about env vars to export.
Required for rootless dockerd to start at boot WITHOUT the user being logged in.
